job_description_info.job_description:
# Cloud Infrastructure / DevOps Contractor – Fleet Connectivity

**Company:** Corvale Mobility (fictional name; intercity rail and coach operator)
**Location:** Kraków, Poland (contract, remote-friendly; occasional office days)
**Engagement:** Service agreement (B2B / freelance), not an employment contract
**Rate:** 95 – 125 PLN per hour

## The engagement

Corvale is preparing a new generation of trains and needs a cloud infrastructure engineer for the team that links the vehicles to the company's cloud platform. You will help shape the architecture from the start and take it to production.

## Scope

- Design, build and operate the cloud infrastructure that links on-board train systems with backend services: telemetry ingestion, alerting, video streaming and remote content updates
- Maintain the infrastructure-as-code repository (Terraform with Terragrunt), keeping it tidy and approachable
- Lead technical proposals across backend and infrastructure from idea to production
- Contribute to system design and challenge decisions with arguments
- Set up secure train-to-cloud communication (mutual TLS, certificate management, network design)
- Agree interfaces and responsibilities with train manufacturers' engineers
- Support backend developers in deploying services that are easy to monitor and run
- Keep the platform observable, reliable and secure

## Requirements

- Hands-on infrastructure engineering and cloud environment design and operation
- AWS preferred; other major clouds acceptable
- Strong Terraform and Terragrunt
- Good understanding of systems architecture and system design
- Networking knowledge, including mTLS and SSL/TLS
- Practical security awareness
- Experience leading technical topics and bringing stakeholders along
- Strong analytical thinking and clear communication

**Nice to have:** IoT or automotive/remote-device integration, backend or full-stack background (JVM preferred), Linux and virtual machines.

## Working model

Independent contractor, invoicing monthly for agreed services.

company_info.company_description:
Corvale Mobility is a privately held transportation and software company headquartered in Kraków, Poland. It operates long-distance bus services and is expanding into passenger rail across Central Europe, supported by an online platform for booking, trip tracking and travel extras. Its asset-light model combines Corvale’s brand, booking technology and network planning with regional operating partners. The company is also investing in a new train fleet and broader use of data and machine learning.

Founded by transport and software professionals, Corvale describes itself as engineering-led, with teams that take end-to-end ownership of their systems. Its stated values are “Lead, Shape, Own, Enjoy the journey,” alongside a focus on technology, sustainability, shared goals and solving problems collaboratively.

The company highlights an international, fast-moving and open-to-ideas culture, with an emphasis on innovation, employee appreciation, professional development and work-life flexibility. Teams are encouraged to shape their work and career paths; employees can work hybrid and may receive travel benefits on Corvale’s network.

Dear Corvale Mobility Hiring Team,

I am applying for the Cloud Infrastructure / DevOps Contractor – Fleet Connectivity role. I bring 10 years of infrastructure experience, including six years operating Kubernetes platforms on AWS, and a track record of shaping reliable cloud platforms from design through production. Corvale’s plans to connect its new train fleet with cloud services make this an especially compelling opportunity to apply that experience to a new, end-to-end system.

At Tallybrook, I lead a five-person platform team operating eight AWS EKS clusters across three regions and approximately 350 services. I built an internal developer platform using service templates, Argo CD and Crossplane-based self-service provisioning, reducing the time to take a new service to production from around two weeks to under a day. I also introduced SLOs and error budgets for critical services, reducing weekly on-call pages by approximately 60%, and moved node provisioning to Karpenter with spot instances, reducing EC2 spend by 38%. These experiences have developed my ability to lead technical work, create practical infrastructure foundations, and help service teams build systems that are observable and operable.

My background also includes managing AWS infrastructure as code in Terraform across approximately 40 modules, using Atlantis for pull-request plan and apply workflows. I have operated systems at scale, replaced noisy monitoring with a Prometheus, Grafana, Alertmanager and Loki stack, and supported capacity planning for game launches serving up to 1.2 million daily active players. Alongside this, my experience with AWS networking and IAM, Linux operations, incident management and technical leadership gives me a strong foundation for contributing to Corvale’s secure and reliable train-to-cloud platform. I would bring an analytical, collaborative approach to system design and technical proposals, while working closely with backend teams and other stakeholders.

I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how my platform engineering and AWS experience could support Corvale Mobility as it takes this fleet connectivity infrastructure from architecture to production. Thank you for your consideration.

Yours sincerely,
Nadia Brennan-Aziz

critique.content_quality_feedback: The cover letter is well structured, professional, concise, and supported by strong quantified evidence: team size, clusters, services, production lead time, on-call reduction, cost reduction, infrastructure modules, and user scale. The progression from platform leadership to broader infrastructure experience is logical. The main content weakness is that several claims are broad or aspirational rather than tied to demonstrated evidence, particularly system design, security, stakeholder alignment, and secure train-to-cloud communication. The letter also does not explicitly explain why the candidate's existing platform experience transfers to fleet connectivity beyond a general reference to Corvale's plans.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The document is highly parseable: it uses standard text, conventional headings, no tables or graphics, and clear contact details. It includes important terms such as AWS, EKS, Terraform, Kubernetes, infrastructure as code, IAM, Linux, observability, reliability, and technical leadership. However, AI/ATS screening probability is moderate to good rather than high because the letter does not contain several central job terms that the candidate's material does not substantiate, including Terragrunt, mTLS, SSL/TLS, certificate management, and train-to-cloud or remote-device integration. Those are candidate gaps rather than wording defects and should not be inserted without evidence. The letter could also use the exact supported term "cloud infrastructure design and operation" more directly and make the existing AWS VPC/IAM experience more visible.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: The candidate is a strong match for hands-on AWS infrastructure operation, Kubernetes platforms, Terraform-based infrastructure as code, observability, reliability, Linux, and technical leadership. The candidate's experience also aligns with the company's engineering-led, ownership-oriented and collaborative culture, although the letter could connect those themes more explicitly to the evidence provided. The principal job-alignment gaps are Terragrunt, mutual TLS/SSL/TLS and certificate management, secure train-to-cloud communication, and IoT, automotive or remote-device integration. The material also does not establish a backend/JVM background. These are substantive experience gaps, not defects that can be solved by rewriting. Stakeholder alignment across external manufacturers is not demonstrated in the supplied candidate information.
